stories.title: UNICEF: 1 in 5 youths targeted by online sexual abuse
stories.summary: The internet is not a safe place for unsupervised children and young people — by now, that's common knowledge. Social media platforms are adept at tweaking their algorithms to ensure users of any age remain on their sites. To do that, they often disseminate content that can be dangerous and upsetting for young people. Studies regularly find a connection between what's known as doomscrolling and a higher risk of psychological problems in the young, including suicidal thoughts. And some of the latest trends in video creation on platforms like TikTok directly endanger the safety of users. In the United States, Meta, which owns both Instagram and Facebook, recently opted to settle a case against it out of court. A number of US states had claimed that the two platforms harmed children. Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion (€14.7 billion) to the states involved and to limit teenagers' access to its platforms to just two hours a day. During the night, access will be completely blocked. A new survey by UNICEF, the UN agency for children, puts the spotlight on another danger that young people constantly face in the digital world: sexual assault, a threat experienced by one in five people between the ages of 12 and 17 over the past year. What are the key findings? The UNICEF report, which DW saw in advance of publication, explains how such attacks often happen.

stories.title: ‘My nude became a sticker’: Hong Kong women say image abuse thrives despite law
stories.summary: Five years after a nude photo was taken without her consent, a woman opened Instagram to find the image had been turned into a sticker and sent back to her in a chat. Terrified that the sticker could already be circulating widely, the victim reached out to Emilia Wong Yue-kiu, a women’s rights activist and adult content creator who advocates for bodily autonomy. But Wong was pessimistic that reporting the case would help, noting it was just one of countless similar messages for help she had...
